subject: E2E latency gating — follow-up & demo checks for Orchid Health migration
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ward <alex.ward@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: latency targets, traffic envelope, next steps

Alex — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the demo: 

What we heard (your targets)
- P95 e2e (app -> Redwood hosted -> app): <= 120ms
- P99 e2e: <= 420ms
- Peak sustained throughput: ~250 reqs/min for the NLU route, with short bursts to 600 reqs/min
- Streaming: up to 40 concurrent streaming sessions during live-scribe flows; typical session length ~9s

Open clarifications we flagged
- Traffic shape: 70% short-form (<=30 tokens), 30% long-form (avg 220 tokens) — please confirm distribution for the demo window
- Tokenization: confirm whether you use byte-pair or sentencepiece for the client-side pre-tokenization (impacts token counts and cost estimates)

Proposed next steps
1) Demo window: Wed 6/14, 10:00–11:30 PT — live demo + directed probe (we run a controlled traffic pass and collect traces).
2) Engineering handoff: Aditya to provision a dedicated test pool with quantized variant + streaming tuned settings for the probe.
3) Deliverables: We will share a short test plan (attached: orchid_latency_plan_v1.xlsx) and a sample trace collection script.
4) Contract/pricing: we will surface an initial fit pricing sheet after the probe results.

If that timeline works, we’ll schedule the demo invite and confirm the traffic profile you want us to exercise.

Attachments: orchid_latency_plan_v1.xlsx (test plan outline, metrics to capture)

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0172
From: Alex Ward <alex.ward@orchidhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: platform@orchidhealth.com
Date: 2028-06-10T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: latency targets, traffic envelope, next steps

Ben — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick items: 

- Confirming the P95/P99 targets above are our internal goals; happy to see what you observe in the probe.
- Traffic distribution: our production mix is closer to 60% short / 40% long; long-form sessions skew towards embeddings + summarization flows.
- Streaming detail: concurrent sessions can spike to ~60 for short periods (peak 3–5 min windows) during clinician note-taking — would you be able to validate 60 concurrent in the canary?

Two asks before Wed: can you share the expected request-level headers/metrics you need from our side (client-side timing hooks, unique request IDs)? Also, include whether the hosted path introduces any additional TLS handshakes that could affect cold-start tail.

Thanks — I’ll confirm availability for 6/14 after I check with the platform team.

— Alex
Alex Ward
CTO (interim) — Orchid Health
alex.ward@orchidhealth.com
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-10T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: orchestration for Orchid probe + demo prep

Ben / Aditya — looping in an internal checklist and owners so we can move fast once Alex confirms: 

Action items
- Ben: finalize traffic profile with Alex (short/long mix = 60/40, peak concurrency targets = 60 streaming sessions). Owner: Ben. Due: EOD 6/11.
- Aditya: provision dedicated test pool (2 x A100 equivalent), enable prefix & KV caching, and create a quantized model variant that matches the accuracy envelope in the plan. Capture kernel selection and quant settings in the handoff doc. Owner: Aditya. Target: ready by 6/13 09:00 PT.
- Priya: prepare the measurement rubric and post-probe acceptance checklist (p95/p99, success-rate, error budget, CPU/GPU utilization thresholds). I’ll upload the rubric to the Drive link and paste the HubSpot probe task.

Notes on measurement & SLO gating
- For the p95 baseline we will use client-observed end-to-end (request timestamp at client send -> server final token delivered). For p99 we will include cold-start and TLS-related tail to reflect production risk.
- Acceptance gates (preliminary): p95 <= 120ms; p99 <= 420ms; streaming median token lag <= 80ms; <1% 5xx error rate; tail retries <= 0.5%

Attached: streaming-handoff.md (internal runbook), kpi-prompts.csv (sample prompt set we’ll use for fidelity checks). I also added the HubSpot probe task: https://hubspot.company/record/ORCHID-2028-01

Ben — when you get Alex’s confirmation we’ll slot the demo and I’ll run the acceptance checklist live with the probe.

Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0124
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-11T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: orchestration for Orchid probe + demo prep

Ack — will provision the pool and validate a canary run at 10 RPS sustained with an injected 60-concurrency streaming spike window (3 x 4-min spikes). I’ll post the alloc + trace endpoints to the Drive link when ready.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Engineering — Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
